evidence.reference_title: DDX41 resolves G-quadruplexes to maintain erythroid genome integrity and prevent cGAS-mediated cell death.
evidence.snippet: Our findings are consistent with this report, as we also observed impaired G4 unwinding activity of the R525H mutant in our FRET-based assays

nodes.description: DDX41 binds 5' splice sites and coordinates splicing with transcriptional elongation. Its loss prevents splicing-coupled RNA polymerase II pausing, allowing R-loops to accumulate and collide with replication forks. Cells enter mitosis with under-replicated DNA and form micronuclei.
nodes.id: Splicing-Coupled R-Loop Accumulation and Replication Stress

evidence.reference_title: DDX41 coordinates RNA splicing and transcriptional elongation to prevent DNA replication stress in hematopoietic cells.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that loss of DDX41 function impairs efficient RNA splicing, resulting in DNA replication stress with excess R-loop formation.

evidence.reference_title: Inherited and Somatic Defects in DDX41 in Myeloid Neoplasms.
evidence.snippet: DDX41 lesions caused altered pre-mRNA splicing and RNA processing.

nodes.description: GeneReviews lists therapy-related myeloid neoplasms with MDS and AML as the most common myeloid neoplasms in carriers. Whether the germline variant raises risk after cytotoxic therapy beyond the baseline carrier risk has not been quantified in the cited sources.

evidence.reference_title: DDX41-Associated Familial Myelodysplastic Syndrome and Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
evidence.snippet: The most common myeloid neoplasms include MDS, AML, and therapy-related myeloid neoplasms.

nodes.description: Isolated thrombocytopenia is a presenting cytopenia in some carriers before neoplasia.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence of cytopenia(s) and somatic variants in patients with DDX41 mutant germline predisposition syndrome.
evidence.snippet: most patients first presented with macrocytic anaemia (n = 5, 42.0%), followed by thrombocytopenia (n = 4, 33.0%), neutropenia (n = 3, 25.0%) or pancytopenia (n = 2, 17.0%)

nodes.description: Homozygous ddx41 loss-of-function zebrafish develop anemia from defective erythroid progenitor expansion and differentiation.

Genome instability in DDX41-deficient hematopoietic cells activates cGAS-STING, and in the hematopoietic-specific knockout mouse this, rather than p53, accounts for lethality. Lymphoblastoid lines and blood from germline carriers show altered inflammation-associated proteins, but whether cGAS-STING signaling is raised in heterozygous human marrow has not been shown.

evidence.reference_title: DDX41 resolves G-quadruplexes to maintain erythroid genome integrity and prevent cGAS-mediated cell death.
evidence.snippet: In parallel, genome instability also activates the cGas-Sting pathway, impairing survival, as cGas deficiency rescues the lethality of hematopoietic-specific Ddx41 knockout mice.

evidence.reference_title: Overall cancer risk in people with deleterious germline DDX41 variants.
evidence.snippet: Finally, both lymphoblastoid cell lines and primary peripheral blood from individuals with germline DDX41LoF variants exhibited differential levels of inflammation-associated proteins.

nodes.description: Somatic helicase-motif VI missense variant acquired in trans in the myeloid clone of germline carriers; the dominant somatic second hit. Not a germline predisposition allele in this syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Biological implications of somatic DDX41 p.R525H mutation in acute myeloid leukemia.
evidence.snippet: The acquired mutation in DDX41 is highly concentrated at c.G1574A (p.R525H) in the conserved motif VI located at the C-terminus of the helicase core domain where ATP interacts and is hydrolyzed.

nodes.description: Germline DDX41 missense variant; the most common germline allele in a Korean cohort.

Transplant stress of Ddx41 heterozygous marrow upregulates p53 targets in erythroid progenitors and impairs HSPC fitness. Halving p53 restores fitness but lets transformed clones emerge, so p53 activation both constrains and selects.

animal_models.description: Transplant stress exposes HSPC fitness defects with p53 target upregulation, and Trp53 reduction rescues fitness.
animal_models.genotype: Ddx41 +/f;Vav-iCre (hematopoietic Ddx41 heterozygous), alone or with Trp53 heterozygous deletion
animal_models.name: Hematopoietic Ddx41 heterozygous mice with and without Trp53 heterozygosity

evidence.reference_title: DDX41 haploinsufficiency causes inefficient hematopoiesis under stress and cooperates with p53 mutations to cause hematologic malignancy.
evidence.snippet: However, stress induced by transplantation of the Ddx41+/- BM resulted in hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell (HSPC) defects and onset of hematopoietic failure upon aging.

evidence.reference_title: DDX41 haploinsufficiency causes inefficient hematopoiesis under stress and cooperates with p53 mutations to cause hematologic malignancy.
evidence.snippet: The reduction in p53 expression rescued the fitness defects in HSPC caused by Ddx41 heterozygosity. However, the combined Ddx41 and Trp53 mutant mice were prone to developing hematologic malignancies that resemble human myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia.
